claims.reason: `[Nonempty ι]` is a binder of the theorem itself, and nothing else in the statement uses it. `W1p`, `W1p0`, `UniformlyEllipticOn`, `energyFormH1`, `preciseRepresentative` and `HolderOnWith` all elaborate without it, so deleting it is a pure deletion. If ι is empty, `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι = PiLp 2 (fun _ => ℝ)` has at most one point, since two points have no coordinate to differ on. If no `Subsingleton` instance is found automatically, it follows from `PiLp`/`WithLp` extensionality together with `isEmptyElim`. So every `K` is subsingleton. I checked that `Set.Subsingleton.holderOnWith` exists in Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Holder.lean with signature `(hs : s.Subsingleton) (C r : ℝ≥0) (f : X → Y) : HolderOnWith C r f s`. Taking α = 1 (so 0 < α ≤ 1) and C = 0 closes the empty case without using the other hypotheses. In the nonempty case, case analysis supplies the `Nonempty ι` instance and the existing proof via `..._of_isCompact_drift` (which itself takes `[Nonempty ι]`) goes through unchanged. Splitting on `isEmpty_or_nonempty ι` therefore gives a proof without the binder.
